options.content:
# 🖥️ GPU Monitoring — Guidance

Quick reference for understanding **GPU, CPU, memory and overall system health**.

🟢 **Healthy**     🟡 **Warning**     🟠 **Critical**     🔴 **Emergency**     ⚪ **Idle**

> 💡 **High GPU utilization is not a problem by itself.**  
> 90–100% utilization can be completely normal during AI training, inference, rendering, or other demanding workloads.

---

## 📊 Metrics & Thresholds

| Metric | What it means | 🟢 Healthy | 🟡 Warning | 🟠 Critical | 🔴 Emergency |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 🌡️ **GPU Temperature** | GPU core temperature | <= 84°C | 85°C | 86°C | ≥ 87°C |
| ⚡ **GPU Utilization** | GPU compute currently in use | 0–100%* | — | — | — |
| 🧠 **VRAM Usage** | GPU memory currently occupied | < 85% | 85–94% | 95–97% | ≥ 98% |
| ⏱️ **GPU Clock** | Current GPU operating frequency | Context-dependent | — | — | — |
| 🔌 **GPU Power** | Current GPU power draw | < 69W | ≥ 69W | ≥ 70W | ≥ 72W |
| 🔄 **PCIe RX** | Data moving Host → GPU | Activity metric | — | — | — |
| 🔄 **PCIe TX** | Data moving GPU → Host | Activity metric | — | — | — |
| 💻 **CPU Usage** | Current processor utilization | < 80% | 80–94% | ≥ 95% | — |
| 🖥️ **RAM Usage** | Current system RAM utilization | < 80% | 80–89% | ≥ 90% | — |

**\*** High GPU utilization is normally healthy if temperature, clock, power, and memory remain within acceptable ranges.

> ⚪ **Low GPU clock while IDLE is normal.**  
> ⚠️ Low clock matters mainly when the GPU is under sustained load.

---

## ❤️ Overall System Health

The overall score combines the main monitored components:

**🎮 GPU Health — 70%**  
**💻 CPU Health — 20%**  
**🧠 Memory Health — 10%**

### Formula

**Overall Health = (GPU × 70%) + (CPU × 20%) + (Memory × 10%)**

GPU health has the largest impact because this system is primarily designed for **GPU-intensive workloads**.

---

## 🩺 GPU Status Guide

| Status | Meaning | Recommended Action |
|---|---|---|
| 🟢 **ACTIVE — HEALTHY** | GPU is under sustained workload and operating normally | No action required |
| ⚪ **IDLE** | No meaningful GPU workload is running | Normal |
| 🟡 **HIGH TEMPERATURE** | GPU temperature requires attention | Check cooling and airflow |
| 🟡 **REDUCED CLOCK** | Clock is lower than expected while under load | Check temperature and power |
| 🟠 **VRAM PRESSURE** | GPU memory usage is high | Reduce memory usage |
| 🟠 **VRAM CRITICAL** | GPU memory is almost exhausted | Reduce batch/model memory immediately |
| 🟠 **POSSIBLE POWER THROTTLING** | Power may be limiting GPU performance | Check power draw and GPU clock |
| 🔴 **POSSIBLE THERMAL THROTTLING** | High temperature may be reducing performance | Reduce workload and inspect cooling |
| 🔴 **EMERGENCY** | Unsafe GPU condition detected | Stop workload and investigate |

---

## 🔎 How to Read GPU Behaviour

| What You See | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| ⚡ High Utilization + 🌡️ Normal Temp + ⏱️ Normal Clock | 🟢 **Healthy heavy workload** |
| ⏱️ Low Clock + ⚪ Idle GPU | ⚪ **Normal power saving** |
| ⚡ High Utilization + ⏱️ Low Clock + 🌡️ High Temp | 🔴 **Possible thermal throttling** |
| ⚡ High Utilization + ⏱️ Low Clock + 🔌 High Power | 🟠 **Possible power limitation** |
| 🧠 Very High VRAM | 🟠 **Memory pressure / possible OOM risk** |
| 🌡️ High Temp + Normal Clock | 🟡 **Cooling requires attention** |

---

## 🌡️ GPU Temperature

- 🟢 **< 85°C** — Healthy
- 🟡 **85–86°C** — Warning
- 🟠 **87–89°C** — Critical
- 🔴 **≥ 90°C** — Emergency

Temperature should always be interpreted together with **GPU utilization and clock**.

---

## ⚡ GPU Utilization

GPU Utilization shows how much of the GPU compute capability is currently being used.

- **0–20%** — Light or idle activity
- **20–80%** — Moderate workload
- **80–100%** — Heavy workload

> 🟢 **100% utilization is not an error.**

High utilization is usually desirable during AI training and other compute-intensive workloads.

---

## 🧠 VRAM Usage

VRAM is the GPU's dedicated memory used by models, tensors, datasets, activations and CUDA workloads.

- 🟢 **< 85%** — Healthy
- 🟡 **85–94%** — Pressure
- 🟠 **95–97%** — Critical
- 🔴 **≥ 98%** — Emergency

Very high VRAM usage may cause **CUDA Out of Memory (OOM)** errors.

Possible actions:

**Reduce batch size → reduce model size → use mixed precision → reduce cached tensors**

---

## ⏱️ GPU Clock

GPU clock changes automatically according to:

**Workload • temperature • power • GPU power state**

### Important

⚪ **Idle + Low Clock** → Normal  
🟢 **Active + Normal Clock** → Healthy  
🟡 **High Load + Reduced Clock** → Investigate  
🔴 **High Load + Reduced Clock + High Temp** → Possible thermal throttling

Low clock alone should **not** be treated as a fault.

---

## 🔌 GPU Power

GPU power normally increases with workload.

- 🟢 **< 69W** — Normal
- 🟡 **≥ 69W** — High
- 🟠 **≥ 70W** — Critical attention
- 🔴 **≥ 72W** — Critical power condition

Power should be interpreted together with **GPU utilization and clock**.

Possible power throttling is suspected when:

**High utilization + Reduced clock + High power**

---

## 🔄 PCIe Throughput

PCIe throughput shows data movement between the system and GPU.

### 📥 RX
**Host → GPU**

Examples:
- dataset transfer
- system RAM → VRAM
- model/tensor transfer

### 📤 TX
**GPU → Host**

Examples:
- results returning to CPU
- tensor output transfer
- processed data returning to system RAM

PCIe RX/TX are primarily **activity/performance indicators**, not health indicators.

---

## 💻 CPU Usage

- 🟢 **< 80%** — Healthy
- 🟡 **80–94%** — High load
- 🟠 **≥ 95%** — Very high sustained load

Temporary high CPU utilization can be normal.

---

## 🖥️ RAM Usage

- 🟢 **< 80%** — Healthy
- 🟡 **80–89%** — High memory usage
- 🟠 **≥ 90%** — Critical memory pressure

Very high RAM usage may cause the operating system to use swap and reduce system performance.

---

## 🛠️ Quick Troubleshooting

| Problem | First Check | Recommended Action |
|---|---|---|
| 🌡️ **High GPU Temp** | Cooling + airflow | Improve cooling / reduce load |
| 🧠 **High VRAM** | Batch/model memory | Reduce batch size / memory usage |
| ⏱️ **Low Clock Under Load** | Temperature + power | Check for throttling |
| 🔌 **High Power** | Power + clock | Check power limitation |
| 🔴 **Thermal Throttling** | Temperature + clock | Reduce workload and inspect cooling |
| 💻 **High CPU** | Running processes | Identify CPU-heavy tasks |
| 🖥️ **High RAM** | Running applications | Reduce memory consumption |
| 🔴 **Emergency** | GPU status + temperature + VRAM | Stop workload and investigate immediately |

---

## 🚦 Quick Diagnostic Rule

### 🟢 Usually Healthy
**High Utilization + Safe Temperature + Normal Clock + Available VRAM**

### 🟡 Needs Attention
**High Temperature OR High Memory OR Unexpected Reduced Clock**

### 🟠 Possible Performance Limitation
**High Utilization + Reduced Clock + High Power/Temperature**

### 🔴 Immediate Investigation
**Emergency Temperature OR Critical GPU Condition**

---

## 💡 Remember

> **High usage does not mean unhealthy hardware.**
>
> A healthy GPU can operate at very high utilization for long periods.
>
> The important question is whether the GPU can maintain its workload while keeping **temperature, clock, power and memory within acceptable operating conditions**.
